packageRules.description: Automerge every update that keeps the major version, 0.x included, once the checks pass and minimumReleaseAge has elapsed

A major update is reviewed by the owner unless a later rule says otherwise. Its PRs stay open until then, so they get a lower prConcurrentLimit than the default 10: the limit is compared against the count of every open Renovate PR, so PRs waiting for review stop being raised at 5 and the other 5 slots stay free for updates that automerge
devDependencies do not reach consumers, so their major updates automerge too
GitHub Actions do not reach consumers, so their major updates automerge too

helpers:pinGitHubActionDigestsToSemver already raises each new release of an action as a version update (`# v6` -> `# v6.1.1` with the new commit), which automerges after minimumReleaseAge. The digest update Renovate raises next to it for a floating major tag carries the same commit, but its renovate/stability-days check stays pending forever (#4233, #4389, #4400, #4583): the branch stage reads a releaseTimestamp that a digest update does not carry (https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/issues/45236), and the open PR takes a prConcurrentLimit slot. Exempting digest updates from minimumReleaseAge instead would merge a moved tag without the cooldown

v4 is a maintenance line: it takes vulnerability fixes (vulnerabilityAlerts.enabled overrides this rule, the mechanism of the security:only-security-updates preset) and lock file maintenance (not listed here), and no other update. This also keeps away major updates of production dependencies that would drop Node 18.18+ support (meow 14 and os-locale 8 require Node 20)

Exempt lock file maintenance from the repository-wide PR limits. Major updates waiting for review keep the concurrent limit full, which held back lock file maintenance on dev from 2026-03 onward; it is the only update that refreshes transitive dependencies, because for yarn.lock Renovate's vulnerabilityAlerts PRs cover direct dependencies only

Lock file maintenance delegates resolution to the package manager, so its updates carry no release timestamp; under Renovate 42's default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-required, the repository-wide minimumReleaseAge keeps renovate/stability-days pending forever and the PR never automerges. The cooldown for yarn.lock is enforced by npmMinimalAgeGate in .yarnrc.yml on every base branch instead (https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/#lockfilemaintenance-updates)
Raise the lower bound of ranges in published packages on each update, so a consumer's install cannot dedupe onto a version older than the one we last released against
test-tools is private; its dependencies stay exact like devDependencies

Renovate reads this file from the default branch only, so it also governs the Cargo workspace that exists only on v6. Lock file maintenance regenerates Cargo.lock with every crate at its newest version and bypasses minimumReleaseAge; npm closes that gap inside the package manager (npmMinimalAgeGate in .yarnrc.yml), Cargo has no equivalent until registry.global-min-publish-age (Rust 1.100) is configured on v6. Re-enable once it is.
Separate mise node updates from GitHub Actions node-version
vite is installed only as the required peer of vitest (vitest 5 accepts ^6.4.0 || ^7.0.0 || ^8.0.0), so its minor and patch updates move in the same PR as vitest
A vite major is taken by hand once the vitest peer range admits it: separateMajorMinor gives a group's major its own branch, where vite could arrive alone and outside that range
Do not update engines.vscode — must stay pinned for Cursor and other forks
